comparator.sourceNotes: The first two years develop historical, theoretical and practical philosophy. The third year combines a 30 EC minor, four advanced philosophy electives and a 10 EC thesis with its accompanying course. The examples shown fit the spring elective periods in the study guide.

alternatives.label: Philosophy across history, society and mind
alternatives.concept: Explore philosophical questions about knowledge, mind, freedom and moral responsibility. Build arguments using logic and rhetoric, and use history, literature and political thought to see how those questions change across settings.
alternatives.labelReason: The option combines the five courses in the UCR Philosophy track with political philosophy, logic and interpretive humanities.
progression: Introductory philosophy and rhetoric support later work in formal reasoning, interpretation, emotion, freedom and responsibility.

alternatives.label: Ethics, politics, justice and institutions
alternatives.concept: Study how ethical arguments inform public life. Connect political philosophy and moral theory with rights, criminal justice, constitutional institutions and social movements.
alternatives.labelReason: Ethics and political philosophy supply the main questions, while public law, political institutions and sociology supply the contexts.
alternatives.distinctness: This option differs from the broad option by 82.5 EC each way. Public law, political institutions and sociology replace much of the historical and literary context.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes the advanced law courses. Introductory philosophy and politics support later study of institutions, conflict and justice.

alternatives.label: Mind, language, cognition and artificial intelligence
alternatives.concept: Investigate minds, language and intelligent systems. Study consciousness, identity, emotion and agency through philosophy, then connect those questions with language processing, cognitive science, logic and AI ethics.
alternatives.labelReason: The option integrates philosophical questions about mind, language and agency with cognitive evidence and computation.
alternatives.distinctness: This option differs from the broad option by 90 EC each way. Cognitive science, psycholinguistics and computational methods replace much of the law, politics and history.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics and later cognition courses. Logic, programming and research methods support later work with cognitive and computational models.

selection.assessment: Three related UCR options give a broad philosophical foundation, an applied ethics and politics direction, and a mind and cognition direction. The historically organised approach shares much of the broad option’s philosophical and interpretive work and is not included because three options already meet the limit.

notes.text: Groningen devotes two years to compulsory philosophy, followed by advanced philosophy electives and a required thesis. The UCR options combine philosophy with subjects such as law, literature, psychology and computing, with fewer dedicated courses in the history of philosophy, epistemology and philosophy of science.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen’s Philosophy degree studies how arguments are made and how philosophers approach knowledge, mind, ethics and political life. It combines a sequence in the history of philosophy with advanced electives, a minor and a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore philosophy through three different emphases. One combines philosophy with history and literature, one focuses on ethics and public institutions, and one connects mind and language with cognitive science and AI.
